subject: Request: Residency proof & deletion certification for AuroraFin (SOC 2 evidence)
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@aurorafin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@aurorafin.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Proof of data residency + deletion certification for AuroraFin tenants

Hi Jordan,

Quick one — as part of our SOC 2 evidence pack we need two items from Redwood relating to our AuroraFin tenancy: a report showing current residency locations for AuroraFin customer data (what regions/storage locations are in use today) and a signed deletion certification template confirming that when AuroraFin requests tenant data erasure you provide a verifiable deletion attestation (with logs/timestamps).

Key constraints: we need EU-only residency confirmation (data must be stored in eu-central & eu-west regions only for our production tenants) and the deletion attestation needs to include the operator, timestamp, and proof-of-action (audit/GCP/Azure delete event ID or equivalent).

Can you share a sample attestation doc and the residency mapping by Tuesday (Nov 17)? We can share the formal evidence request if useful.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Compliance — AuroraFin
oliver@aurorafin.com

Attachment: aurorafin_deletion_request.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of data residency + deletion certification for AuroraFin tenants

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Evelyn (Security) and Mina (Data Ops) to confirm the exact artifacts we can provide and the expected format.

High level: we can provide a residency map (per-tenant region markers), a standard deletion-cert template that includes operator, UTC timestamp, and the internal audit log entry id. For cloud delete confirmation we attach cloud provider deletion event IDs where available. We’ll confirm if any redaction is required on the residency export.

Evelyn/Mina — can you confirm the following by EOD Thu (11/12)?
- Per-tenant residency export (CSV/Excel) for AuroraFin production tenants
- Deletion-certification template (we have an existing template) + example filled instance for a previous erasure request
- Whether we can include cloud provider deletion event ids in the attestation, or we provide internal audit IDs mapped to provider events.

Oliver — if there’s a preferred format for the cert (DocuSign-ready PDF or signed Word doc) say so and we’ll prepare it.

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of data residency + deletion certification for AuroraFin tenants

Jordan / Mina — responding with the evidence checklist and open questions.

We can deliver:
- Residency mapping: XLSX that includes tenant_id, tenant_alias, primary_region, secondary_region (if any), storage_bucket_prefix, and retention_policy_ttl_days. We will mark production vs staging.
- Deletion certification: our standard template includes: tenant_id, data_types_covered, request_timestamp_utc, operator (internal id + name), deletion_action_id (our internal audit id), provider_event_id (if available), and an auditor signature line.
- Example: we have a filled example from Jan 2026 for Tenant X (we can sanitize tenant names).

Open questions for AuroraFin:
1) Do you require provider-level event ids (e.g., GCS/Azure Storage delete event) embedded in the certificate, or is an internal audit deletion_action_id sufficient when we map it to the provider event separately?
2) For residency — do you need historical retention (where data lived over the last 12 months) or only current-state mapping?

We will prepare the residency XLSX and the blank + example cert. ETA: Nov 15 COB. I’ll attach the sanitized example once cleared.

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@aurorafin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: AuroraFin Compliance <compliance@aurorafin.com>, Lewis & Partners <procurement@lewispartners.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of data residency + deletion certification for AuroraFin tenants

Evelyn — thanks, that sounds good. Short answers:
1) Provider event ids are preferred where available (helps our cloud audit). If there’s a scenario where they’re not available, an internal deletion_action_id that maps to the provider event is acceptable.
2) Current-state mapping is our priority for the SOC 2 window; we may ask for 12-month historical movement later but not needed for this request.

Format: DocuSign-ready PDF for the cert would be ideal. We’ll take the residency XLSX.

Two small asks: can you include whether the tenant is on Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted (affects who performs deletion) and whether any customer-managed keys (BYOK) are in use?

Oliver

Attachment: residency_map_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@aurorafin.com>, Lewis & Partners <procurement@lewispartners.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of data residency + deletion certification for AuroraFin tenants

Oliver / Lewis — delivering the consolidated response per your requests. See attached package and notes below.

Attachments included:
- residency_map_v2.xlsx (per-tenant current-state residency, production flag, deployment type)
- deletion-cert-template.docx (DocuSign-ready template)
- example_deletion_cert_filled.pdf (sanitized example showing deletion_action_id and provider_event_id mapping)

Summary notes:
- Residency: AuroraFin production tenants currently located in eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 only (columns primary_region, secondary_region are filled). No data stored outside EU regions for listed tenant_ids.
- Deletion certification: our template includes both internal deletion_action_id (redwood-audit-<id>) and provider_event_id where provider emits one. The example file shows the mapping and auditor signature.
- Dedicated vs Hosted: residency_map_v2 includes a deployment_type column (Hosted | Dedicated). Deletions for Dedicated environments are initiated by the customer tenant owner but executed and logged by Redwood's ops with identical audit entries; template accounts for the operator being either "Redwood Ops" or "Customer Admin".
- BYOK: column present; for AuroraFin tenants the BYOK column is "no" for the tenants listed. If you have tenants using BYOK, we will note key-owner and KMS details.

Next steps:
1) If the DocuSign flow is acceptable, confirm a signatory and we’ll send the cert for signature.
2) If you need provider raw event logs attached we can provide a redacted export mapping deletion_action_id->provider_event_id (requires an MSA addendum for raw provider event export; suggest we start an intake if you want that).

Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the package.

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Bcc: internal compliance tracker updated (HubSpot 4839201)
